  • Observed at 19:38:17 Eastern time ET
    Paul Pieczynski v. Brian Szumski (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca3-26-01643 / USCOURTS-ca3-26-01643-0

    FAPD-AI: Pieczynski appealed a federal district court's dismissal of his lawsuit against the Luzerne County Sheriff, in which he sought to void a 2016 sheriff's sale and recover property that had been foreclosed upon by Wells Fargo Bank following his 2013 mortgage default. The plaintiff claimed he possessed an 1812 land patent for the property that he had recorded in 2015, prior to the sale. The Third Circuit affirmed the dismissal, holding that Pieczynski's claims were barred by the Rooker-Feldman doctrine, which prevents federal courts from reviewing state court judgments, and that he forfeited arguments regarding other grounds for dismissal by failing to challenge them in his appellate brief. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    PRESACT · web feed · White House Presidential Actions · publisher-dated 2026-09-16

    USA v. Garry Hayes (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-05893 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-05893-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit affirmed a district court's supervised release condition prohibiting Garry Hayes, convicted of transmitting threatening communications to members of Congress, from contacting any member of Congress during his one-year supervised release period. Although the court found the condition overly broad and acknowledged it burdened Hayes's First Amendment rights, it affirmed because Hayes failed to demonstrate plain error, as the condition's unlawfulness was not obvious or clear. The court noted the condition should have been narrower but found the error did not meet the stringent plain error standard. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 17:13:15 Eastern time ET
    Handy, Et AL. V. Jones, Et AL. (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca9-25-5105 / USCOURTS-ca9-25-5105-0

    FAPD-AI: The Ninth Circuit vacated a district court's denial of qualified immunity to four Anchorage police officers who shot Kristopher Handy as he held a shotgun and advanced toward them during a domestic disturbance response. The court held that Handy presented an immediate threat and that the officers' use of deadly force was objectively reasonable under the totality of the circumstances. The court further determined that the officers would be entitled to qualified immunity because the alleged constitutional violation was not a clearly established violation of law at the time of the incident. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-25-05655 / USCOURTS-ca6-25-05655-0

    FAPD-AI: The Sixth Circuit held that a motion challenging an amended judgment created through prior collateral relief is not a "second or successive" motion under 28 U.S.C. § 2255 and remanded for further proceedings. Augustin's prior § 924(c) conviction had been vacated and his sentence amended in an earlier successful § 2255 motion, and the court determined that this amended judgment constituted a new judgment that could be challenged for the first time without the "second or successive" gatekeeping restrictions. The court also denied Augustin's request to reassign the case to a different district judge. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    USA v. Silverio Henriquez, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca11-23-13425 / USCOURTS-ca11-23-13425-0

    FAPD-AI: The Eleventh Circuit affirmed the drug trafficking convictions of two defendants prosecuted under the Maritime Drug Law Enforcement Act for conspiracy and possession of cocaine aboard a stateless vessel in the Dominican Republic's Exclusive Economic Zone. The court rejected their arguments that the statute was unconstitutional as applied to conduct occurring in the exclusive economic zone rather than the high seas, and found no violation of Federal Rules of Criminal Procedure regarding delays in bringing them before a magistrate judge. The case was remanded to correct technical errors in the judgment documents. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Airworthiness Directives; De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (Type Certificate Previously Held by Bombardier, Inc.… (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-09-16 / 2026-18956

    official summary: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain De Havilland Aircraft of Canada Limited (Type Certificate Previously Held by Bombardier, Inc.) Model DHC-8-401 and DHC-8-402 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a report that instructions for fay, fillet, and rivet dome sealing were omitted for a bracket installed on the inboard surface of the tank rib, which could allow fuel to leak from the wing fuel tank into the wing dry bay. This proposed AD would require a detailed visual inspection of the affected bracket assembly for signs of fuel leakage and for the presence of fillet seal and fastener dome seal, and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-02

    official summary: The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (“Commission” or “CFTC”) is amending its rules implementing section 23 of the Commodity Exchange Act (“CEA”). Section 23 of the CEA and the Commission's implementing regulations provide for the payment of awards, subject to certain limitations and conditions, to whistleblowers who provide the Commission with information that aids in successful enforcement efforts. The Commission is adopting amendments, which are modeled on a similar provision in the Securities and Exchange Commission's (“SEC”) regulations, to part 165 of its regulations to increase the efficiency, transparency, and predictability of whistleblower claims process, thereby protecting and enhancing the program's effectiveness in incentivizing whistleblowers to report. The amendments also include technical corrections to the whistleblower rules to reflect the Whistleblower Office's (“WBO”) move in 2025, consistent with its adjudicatory functions, to the Office of the General Counsel (“OGC”). FR-SEL-01

    official summary: This document provides a notice of public hearing on the notice of proposed rulemaking (REG-119986-25) published in the Federal Register on September 4, 2026. The proposed regulations would update existing regulations to provide that a private school is not described as an organization exempt from Federal income tax if it discriminates on the basis of race, color, or national or ethnic origin in administration of its educational, admissions, scholarship, athletic, or other policies, based on the fundamental public policy of the United States against such practices.     Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-09-16 / 2026-19027

    official summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or the Agency) is proposing to approve Indiana's Coal Combustion Residuals (CCR) partial permit program under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA). After reviewing the CCR permit program application submitted by the Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM), EPA has preliminarily determined that Indiana's CCR permit program meets the standard for partial approval under RCRA. If approved, Indiana's CCR permit program will operate in lieu of the Federal CCR program, with the exception of the specific provisions noted below. EPA is seeking comment on this proposal during a 60-day public comment period and will hold a hybrid in-person and online public hearing on EPA's preliminary approval of Indiana's partial CCR permit program.     Federal Register · govinfo API · FR-2026-09-16 / 2026-19053

    FAPD-AI: The President continues the national emergency declared on September 23, 2001, with respect to persons who commit, threaten to commit, or support terrorism, as strengthened by Executive Order 13886 of September 9, 2019. The continuation extends the emergency measures for one additional year beyond September 23, 2026, based on the determination that such persons continue to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to U.S. national security, foreign policy, and economy. This notice is published in accordance with the National Emergencies Act. FR-SEL-03

    119 HR 9617 RH: Coordinating and Harnessing America’s Recovery of Minerals Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119hr9617rh

    FAPD-AI: The bill directs the EPA Administrator to develop a National Critical Mineral Recovery Strategy coordinating federal efforts to recover critical minerals from discarded materials. The strategy must identify existing programs and authorities, opportunities to expand recovery from mining and processing waste, potential sources and barriers to recovery, and methods to minimize environmental and health risks while strengthening domestic supply chains. The Administrator is required to submit biennial reports to Congress on implementation and recommendations. BILLS-SEL-01

    S759 ENR: Modernizing Access to Our Public Oceans Act (opens in a new tab)
    Legislation · govinfo API · BILLS-119s759enr

    FAPD-AI: This enacted law requires the Secretary of Commerce to develop data standards and make publicly available geographic information system data on fishing restrictions, recreational vessel use and access to federal waters within the exclusive economic zone. The data must be standardized, updated at least twice annually with some data in real time, and organized for public accessibility while excluding sensitive cultural and commercial information. The law directs coordination with federal agencies, states, Indian Tribes, and other stakeholders to ensure data compatibility and interoperability. BILLS-SEL-01
